exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Yes, 11:30! For a reused key with a different body, the IETF idempotency-key draft says 422; a missing key on an endpoint that requires one is 400, and a repeat while the first is still running is 409. Store a hash of the request body with the key so you can tell. We'll walk through the unique constraint together.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Exception note, Dependabot #212 (GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw, urllib3 < 2.8.0, High). Opened 9/30/2026; SLA 30 days (10/30); remediated 11/5 (urllib3 2.8.0, PR #1498, deployed 10:40 CT), 6 days late. Why late: the alert wasn't triaged during the on-call rotation (noted in the 10/30 handoff but not owned). Exposure: billing-worker streams webhook responses from tenant-configured URLs, so it was reachable by a malicious tenant endpoint. Evidence of no exploitation: no OOM kills or memory spikes on the webhook pool 9/30-11/5 (Datadog). Change: Dependabot High/Critical alerts are assigned to the on-call engineer within 2 business days, with a weekly SLA check in the Billing standup.
